title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 48-50). Grothendieck takes P., the category of complexes of free finite-type Λ-modules that are quasi-isomorphic to suitable bounded complexes. He equips it with Σ., the class of degreewise exact (hence degreewise split) short exact sequences, and with a distinguished cochain complex C^·_· of objects of P. His aim is to show that (P., C^·_·, Σ.) solves a universal problem.

On p.48 he axiomatizes 'a class of exact sequences' Σ in an additive category B:
- Sex1: every sequence in Σ is a kernel-cokernel pair.
- Sex2: Σ is stable under isomorphisms and finite sums, and contains the trivial sequences.
These are the first axioms of an exact category (Quillen 1972/73), or of a 'proper class' in relative homological algebra (Heller, Buchsbaum, Eilenberg-Moore). There is no pullback/pushout axiom.

This page develops the basic vocabulary.
1. A Σ-monomorphism (resp. Σ-epimorphism) is a morphism that occurs as the first (resp. last) map of a sequence in Σ. In modern terms these are admissible monics (inflations) and admissible epics (deflations).
2. A morphism A→B is Σ-strict if it has a kernel P and a cokernel Q with P→A a Σ-mono and B→Q a Σ-epi. He claims this is equivalent to a factorization A→R→B with 0→P→A→R→0 and 0→R→B→Q→0 in Σ. This is the notion of an admissible (strict) morphism in an exact category.
3. He notes that one should perhaps require Σ-monos (resp. Σ-epis) to be closed under composition. This is exactly Quillen's composition axiom, here entering as an afterthought.
4. Σ-projective and Σ-injective objects are defined in the obvious way (relative projectives and injectives).
5. A sequence A→B→C is Σ-special if it splits into short sequences in Σ:
   - 0→Ker→A→Coim→0,
   - 0→Im→Ker(B→C)→H→0,
   - 0→Ker→B→Coim→0, and so on.
   The vertical identifications are Coim(A→B)≅Im(A→B) and Ker(B→C) common to two rows. In modern terms: both differentials are admissible and the homology object H exists, with admissible sequences. He remarks that the notion is self-dual.
6. A complex is Σ-special if all its consecutive pairs are; it is Σ-acyclic if moreover all H^i=0, which is the modern notion of an acyclic complex in an exact category (Neeman 1990, Keller, Bühler 2010).
7. A Σ-resolution of A is a Σ-special cochain complex concentrated in degrees ≥0 with H^i=0 for i≠0 (presumably H^0≅A).

Purpose (next page): Σ-exact k-linear functors P.→B, i.e. those respecting Σ-'moyennes' (admissible image factorizations), should be classified by their value on C^·_·. The restriction functor F↦F(C^·_·) should be fully faithful. Its essential image should be the complexes in B whose differentials have Σ-factorizations, or, in variant (b), the Σ-resolutions. So the category of (perfect) complexes with the degreewise-split exact structure would be the free 'exact-type' category on a complex with admissible differentials, or on a Σ-resolution. This presumably serves the dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures in the title.
errors: Gap in the claimed equivalence 'Σ-strict ⇔ factorization A→R→B through Σ-sequences'. From P→A Σ-mono and B→Q Σ-epi one gets R=Coker(P→A) and R'=Ker(B→Q), but the canonical map Coim→Im (R→R') need not be an isomorphism in a general additive category under only Sex1-Sex2. One must either require Coim≅Im or have more exact-category axioms. The reverse direction is fine using Sex1.

Without the composition (and pullback/pushout) axioms, which he only tentatively suggests, Σ-acyclic complexes and Σ-resolutions behave badly. For example, compositions and comparison of resolutions are not available; the 'peut-être' indicates awareness that the axiom system is incomplete.

Minor inconsistency: the Σ-resolution condition here is H^i=0 for i≠0, while the next page states H^i(C^·)=0 for i≥0 (uncertain reading). This possibly reflects augmented versus non-augmented conventions.

ideas.what: Planned universal property: complexes of free f.t. modules with degreewise-split Σ and a universal complex classify complexes with Σ-admissible differentials / Σ-resolutions in any (B,Σ) via Σ-exact functors
ideas.modern_name: universal property of Ch(proj) as exact category (free exact category on a complex/resolution)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard credit known to me (related: Freyd's free abelian category, Keller 'Chain complexes and stable categories' 1990)

missed.claim: The page sets up the vocabulary for the theorem planned on the next page: (P., C^·_·, Σ.) is universal among triples (B, C^·, Σ) where the differentials admit Σ-factorizations (or where C^· is a Σ-resolution). This would be a universal characterization of the category of perfect/free complexes with the degreewise-split exact structure. I am not aware of this being stated in the literature in this form.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Universal properties of categories of complexes ('free exact/stable category on a complex') bear on K-theory and on presentations of perfect complexes, for instance in additivity and dévissage arguments, and on the universal property of exact categories versus stable ∞-categories.

missed.claim: This is an independent, slightly weaker axiomatization of exact categories (no pullback/pushout axiom; composition axiom only suggested) by Grothendieck ca. 1975-76, together with the notions of admissible morphism and acyclic complex. These notions were made explicit in print only later (Neeman 1990, Bühler 2010).

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck working with exact-category language and relative homological algebra in the context of perfect complexes and dévissage.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of definitions (admissible monos/epis, strict morphisms, acyclic complexes in an exact category) that are standard today and largely due to Quillen, Heller and relative homological algebra. The only potentially interesting element is the universal-property programme it serves, which is stated on the neighbouring page rather than here.
transcription_corrections: The sentence should read: 'Un morphisme A→B est dit Σ-strict, s'il a un noyau P et un conoyau Q, et si P→A (B→Q) est un Σ-mono (Σ-épi)'. It is not 'Un monomorphisme dit strict'; 'strict' is crossed out and replaced by 'Σ-strict' written above.
The sequences begin with '0 →', not '· →' (e.g. '0 → A → B → K → 0', '0 → P → A → R → 0', '0 → R → B → Q → 0').
'Σ-monomorphisme A→B de B' means 'in the category B' (calligraphic B).
The scored-out lines are an earlier attempt: 'Une suite [exacte] dite complexe de cochaînes (discret) ... C^{i-1} → C^i → C^{i+1} est dit spécial'.
The left margin note reads approximately 'définir Σ-épi, Σ-mono' (uncertain).
The vertical ≀ marks denote the identifications Coim(A→B) ≅ Im and Ker(B→C) shared between rows; the last row is '0 → Im → C → Coker(B→C) → 0' (approx.).
